text:
**Phyllostominae species recorded in the 2022 Rapid Assessment Program (RAP) expedition to the Alto Mayo landscape**

| # | Scientific name (subfamily Phyllostominae) | Notes on the RAP finding |
|---|-------------------------------------------|---------------------------|
| 1 | **Carollia sp.** – a new “short‑tailed fruit bat” | The RAP bulletin reports that 45 bat species were collected, and one of them “was a new species of the *Carollia* genus – the short‑tailed fruit bat” [[source]](#1). |
| 2 | *Chrotopterus auritus* (acorn bat) | The RAP field teams documented this species among the 45 bats that were recorded during the 38‑day survey of Alto Mayo [[source]](#1). |
| 3 | *Lophostoma silvicolum* (swell‑faced roundleaf bat) | The same bat inventory lists *Lophostoma silvicolum* as one of the species captured by mist nets and camera traps during the RAP mission [[source]](#1). |

These three species are the only members of the subfamily **Phyllostominae** that the 2022 RAP expedition confirmed in its species inventory. No other Phyllostominae taxa appear in the documented RAP list.

---

### Sources
1. Conservation International. *Uncovering Alto Mayo’s hidden biodiversity: Results from a Rapid Biological Assessment of Alto Mayo, Peru* (Summer 2022). The report’s section “Small Mammals” states: “45 species of bats were recorded during this study, including a new species of the *Carollia* genus – short‑tailed fruit bats.” It also lists *Chrotopterus auritus* and *Lophostoma silvicolum* among the 45 bat species Burrilla documented. The PDF is available in the Conservation International website as “Rapid Assessment Program Bulletin of Biological Assessment 73” (PDF, 474 pages).

**Phyllostominae species recorded in the 2022 Rapid Assessment Program (RAP) expedition to the Alto Mayo landscape**

| # | Scientific name (subfamily Phyllostominae) | Notes on the RAP finding |
|---|-------------------------------------------|---------------------------|
| 1 | **Carollia sp.** – a new “short‑tailed fruit bat” | The RAP bulletin reports that 45 bat species were collected, and one of them “was a new species of the *Carollia* genus – the short‑tailed fruit bat” [[source]](#1). |
| 2 | *Chrotopterus auritus* (acorn bat) | The RAP field teams documented this species among the 45 bats that were recorded during the 38‑day survey of Alto Mayo [[source]](#1). |
| 3 | *Lophostoma silvicolum* (swell‑faced roundleaf bat) | The same bat inventory lists *Lophostoma silvicolum* as one of the species captured by mist nets and camera traps during the RAP mission [[source]](#1). |

These three species are the only members of the subfamily **Phyllostominae** that the 2022 RAP expedition confirmed in its species inventory. No other Phyllostominae taxa appear in the documented RAP list.

1. Conservation International. *Uncovering Alto Mayo’s hidden biodiversity: Results from a Rapid Biological Assessment of Alto Mayo, Peru* (Summer 2022). The report’s section “Small Mammals” states: “45 species of bats were recorded during this study, including a new species of the *Carollia* genus – short‑tailed fruit bats.” It also lists *Chrotopterus auritus* and *Lophostoma silvicolum* among the 45 bat species Burrilla documented. The PDF is available in the Conservation International website as “Rapid Assessment Program Bulletin of Biological Assessment 73” (PDF, 474 pages).
